audit.why: Olaf wins 1-2 on a landed axe and loses every extended trade from 3 onward — consistent with 53.71% over 1,508 games.
audit.corrected: Kept; the mechanics that decide each stage were added.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike said Ragnarok "makes him CC-immune, so your knockup won’t stop him" — an absolute that is not true.
audit.why: Riot's text: he becomes "immune to disables for as long as he keeps attacking" (100/90/80s). The immunity is conditional on him swinging, so disengaging or peeling him off a target ends it. Telling a player their knockup simply does not work removes their actual out.
audit.corrected: spikes[1] and mid now state the attacking condition and the peel that follows from it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important rule in the matchup was missing: Undertow resets its own cooldown when Olaf picks the axe up.
audit.why: Riot's text: "If Olaf picks up the axe, the ability's cooldown is reset." "Dodge the axe" is therefore incomplete advice — the punish window only exists if you also deny the pickup by moving away from where it landed. Undertow also reduces Armor, which the page never mentioned.
audit.corrected: spikes[0], early and wants.you[0] now say to step off the axe, and early states the armour shred.

edits.before: Dodge his axe (Q, Undertow) to kill his slow and reset — a whiffed axe means he can't stick to you, so E away, then re-engage on your terms with the Q pattern.
edits.after: Dodging Undertow (Q) is not enough — if he picks the axe back up the cooldown resets, so step away from the axe, not just the throw, then re-engage on your terms.

edits.before: Olaf is dangerous and ahead Level 1-2 if he lands Undertow (Q) — the slow lets him stick and stack Reckless Swing true damage before you have a Q pattern or E lifesteal to answer. The whole matchup pivots on dodging that axe: a missed Undertow strips his slow and lets you disengage or re-position. Farm carefully, don't get chunked by free axe hits, and don't fight into his slow. He's favoured here because his early fury sustain and true damage out-trade your raw kit before you spike.
edits.after: Olaf is dangerous and ahead level 1-2 if he lands Undertow (Q) — it slows you AND cuts your armour, letting him stick and stack Reckless Swing true damage before you have a Q pattern or E lifesteal. But the axe is only half of it: picking it back up resets the cooldown outright, so walk away from where it landed, not just out of the throw. Farm carefully and don't fight into the slow; his Berserker Rage attack speed and lifesteal both grow as he drops low.

edits.before: Dodge Undertow (Q) to deny his slow and stick
edits.after: Step off the axe — a pickup resets Undertow

edits.before: From Level 3 your drain fighter kit out-sustains Olaf's fury healing in a long brawl. You want extended trades — E lifesteal plus Q3 sweetspots simply out-heal Reckless Swing over time. Bait his Undertow into a minion, then commit. At 6, respect that Ragnarok makes him immune to your knockup, so don't rely on the sweetspot to peel him; instead trade straight up, because World Ender's heal amp wins the sustained DPS race even through his ult.
edits.after: From level 3 your drain out-sustains Olaf's missing-health lifesteal in a long brawl. You want extended trades — E lifesteal plus Q3 sweetspots out-heal Reckless Swing, which costs him health too unless it kills. Bait Undertow into a minion and step off the axe, then commit. At 6, Ragnarok makes him immune to disables only for as long as he keeps attacking, so peeling him off with W still works the moment he stops swinging.

edits.before: Olaf's Ragnarok makes him CC-immune, so your knockup won't stop him — but World Ender's heal amp lets you out-drain his Reckless Swing during his ult, so trade through it and win the DPS race.
edits.after: Ragnarok makes him immune to disables only while he keeps attacking, so your knockup lands the moment he stops — and World Ender's heal amp out-drains Reckless Swing through the ult, so trade and win.

notes: Olaf's W is Tough It Out (attack speed + shield, 16/15/14/13/12s); the page's "fury sustain" is really Berserker Rage, the passive missing-health lifesteal, and is now named. Aatrox's Infernal Chains (W) carries a derived "grounding" flag Riot's description does not support (drag + slow only); no grounding claim was made in this slice.
